answer: Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 53% of the attester's bond. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the forge registry records each claim and the summit audit publishes every slash. A farm must hence either lie, which the bridge graph proves on replay, or recruit 26 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. That is 29 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
